questions.q: What does the summary mean by neuroadaptation?
a: The brain builds tolerance and needs more for the same pleasure
The brain rewires itself to dislike all pleasure
Nerve damage caused by too much screen time
The habit of switching between different addictions
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that repeated dopamine hits make the brain resistant, so more of the source is required.

questions.q: What does the summary say always follows pleasure?
a: Pain
Rest
Guilt
Boredom
questions.why: Lesson 2 states plainly that pleasure is not free, because pain follows it.

questions.q: Which activities does the summary give as healthy sources of pain?
a: Exercise, fasting, and cold showers
Gambling, gaming, and browsing
Shopping, snacking, and streaming
Meditation, journaling, and reading
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists workouts, intermittent fasting, and cold showers as pain that leads to lasting benefit.

questions.q: What is the first step to stopping overindulgence, according to the summary?
a: Restricting your access to tempting stimuli
Tracking how much pleasure you feel
Replacing one addiction with another
Avoiding all contact with other people
questions.why: Lesson 1 says that because dopamine temptations surround us, you must limit how easily you can reach them.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest doing when you feel stressed instead of reaching for a distraction?
a: Identify the distress your mind is covering up
Distract yourself with music or a podcast
Wait until the feeling passes on its own
Talk about it with a professional
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends listening to your inner voice and finding the source of the misery you are avoiding.
